message.content:
Based on my search, here is a comprehensive overview of BMI (Body Mass Index) standards used worldwide:

## What is BMI?

BMI is a screening measure calculated as **weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared** (kg/m²). It provides an estimate of body fat and is widely used to categorize weight status and assess potential health risks.

---

## Standard BMI Classifications (WHO/CDC/NIH - Used for White, Hispanic, and Black populations)

| Category | BMI Range |
|----------|-----------|
| Underweight | Less than 18.5 |
| Healthy/Normal weight | 18.5 to 24.9 |
| Overweight | 25.0 to 29.9 |
| Obesity Class I | 30.0 to 34.9 |
| Obesity Class II | 35.0 to 39.9 |
| Obesity Class III (Severe Obesity) | 40.0 or greater |

These classifications are based on cardiovascular disease risk and have been adopted by the **National Institutes of Health (NIH)** and **World Health Organization (WHO)** for general adult populations.

---

## Asian-Specific BMI Standards

Research shows that people of Asian descent experience metabolic complications at lower BMI levels. The WHO and various Asian health organizations recommend **lower thresholds**:

| Category | BMI Range |
|----------|-----------|
| Underweight | Less than 18.5 |
| Normal | 18.5 to 22.9 |
| Overweight | 23.0 to 24.9 |
| Obese | 25.0 or greater |

For example:
- **Singapore's guidelines**: Healthy range is 18.5–22.9 kg/m²; overweight starts at 23.0; obesity at 27.5
- **NHS (UK) adjustments**: South Asian descent – BMI ≥ 27.5; Chinese, Black African, or African-Caribbean – BMI ≥ 28.0

---

## China's National BMI Standards

According to China's National Health Commission (2024 weight management guidelines):

| Category | BMI Range |
|----------|-----------|
| Underweight (体重过低) | Less than 18.5 |
| Normal (体重正常) | 18.5 to 23.9 |
| Overweight (超重) | 24.0 to 27.9 |
| Obese (肥胖) | 28.0 or greater |

**Special considerations for China:**
- **Central obesity** (中心型肥胖): Men ≥ 90 cm waist circumference; Women ≥ 85 cm
- **Elderly (80+ years)**: Recommended BMI range is **22.0–26.9 kg/m²**

---

## Important Limitations of BMI

BMI is a **screening tool**, not a diagnostic measure of body fat or health. It does not account for:
- **Muscle mass** (athletes may have high BMI but low body fat)
- **Fat distribution** (visceral fat is more dangerous than subcutaneous fat)
- **Age, sex, and ethnicity**
- **Bone density**

For a more complete health assessment, BMI should be considered alongside:
- **Waist circumference**
- **Body fat percentage**
- **Blood pressure, cholesterol, and glucose levels**
- **Overall fitness and medical history**

---

## Clinical and Surgical Eligibility Examples

| Context | BMI Threshold |
|---------|---------------|
| General obesity diagnosis (standard) | ≥ 30 |
| Bariatric surgery (standard) | ≥ 35, or ≥ 30 with comorbidities |
| Bariatric surgery (Asian patients) | ≥ 27.5 |
| Weight-loss medications (e.g., Zepbound/Tirzepatide) | ≥ 30, or ≥ 27 with weight-related conditions |

---

Sources:
1. https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/articles/9464-body-mass-index-bmi
2. https://www.heart.org/en/healthy-living/healthy-eating/losing-weight/bmi-in-adults
3. https://www.myheart.org.sg/tools-resources/bmi-calculator/
4. https://www.uptodate.com/contents/image?imageKey=OBGYN%2F97661
5. http://www.nhc.gov.cn/ylyjs/s3573d/202412/4cf1905d32304c15ac3bc4446ddb83f1/files/f932c5c0004f4959b92613dd1024483c.pdf
6. http://dayi.org.cn/qa/279026
7. https://www.chinacdc.cn/jkkp/mxfcrb/lnjk/202408/t20240823_295135.html
8. https://www.cdc.gov/bmi/adult-calculator/bmi-categories.html
9. https://www.boltpharmacy.co.uk/guide/low-bmi-gastric-sleeve
10. https://www.trimbodymd.com/faqs/zepbound-bmi-requirements/
11. https://bmicalculatorweb.com/blog/who-new-bmi-classification-obesity-diagnosis-criteria.html
12. https://carelyclinic.com/gastric-sleeve-eligibility-criteria/
13. https://biologyinsights.com/bmi-cutoffs-the-standard-categories-and-health-risks/
14. https://www.peptidepro.co.uk/tirzepatide-nhs-eligibility-bmi-guide-2026/
